summary.business_problem: Current payment processing lacks secure, compliant, and resilient integration with a payment provider, exposing the system to PCI-DSS violations and operational failures during high load or service outages.
summary.proposed_solution: Integrate Stripe as the sole payment provider to enable secure, hosted card entry, ensure all payment state transitions are audited immutably, and implement resilient, idempotent webhook processing to maintain order integrity and compliance under normal and failure conditions.

in_scope: Integrate with Stripe for card payments as the only payment provider in this release.
Create a payment record in 'pending' state before redirecting the customer to the payment provider.
Expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe.
Verify incoming webhook callbacks using Stripe's signature scheme with a shared secret configured at deployment time.
Handle out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries using a delivery ID derived from the payload and validated against a known list of processed IDs with timestamps.
If a payment fails, mark the order as 'payment failed' and allow the customer to retry payment with the same order.
Record the provider's failure reason code for every failed payment attempt.
Support agents must be able to issue full or partial refunds for completed payments, with refunds not exceeding the original captured amount.
Notify customers by email via SMTP in HTML format when a refund is issued, including a clear statement such as 'Your refund of $X has been issued for order #Y.'
Record every payment state transition (e.g., pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded) in an immutable audit log with a timestamp and actor identification.
Ensure payment audit logs are retained for a minimum of 7 years to meet financial compliance requirements.
Process incoming webhook callbacks within 2 seconds under normal load, defined as 100 concurrent requests per second.
Ensure the system is resilient to temporary Stripe API unavailability by not losing orders during such events.
out_of_scope: Supporting any payment provider other than Stripe.
Storing raw card numbers in the system or any form of cardholder data.
Implementing or managing any third-party payment gateway outside of Stripe.
Developing or integrating any payment processing feature beyond card payments via Stripe.
Implementing or managing any refund processing outside of the 'captured' state.
future_scope: Extending payment processing to support additional payment methods beyond card payments.
Implementing real-time fraud detection or risk scoring for transactions.
Adding support for recurring payments or subscription models.
assumptions: The e-commerce platform supports online payments for customer orders.
The platform can support asynchronous callbacks from Stripe via webhook endpoints.
constraints: Payment processing depends on the order-creation flow being completed first.
Refunds are only allowed when a payment has reached the 'captured' state and has not undergone any further state changes.
Raw card numbers must not be stored in the system; all card entry occurs via Stripe-hosted fields.
Webhook signature verification depends on a shared secret configured with Stripe at deployment time.
The payment audit log must be stored in encrypted, append-only database entries with immutable timestamps and actor identification.

epics.title: Integrate with Stripe for Card Payments
epics.objective: Establish secure, compliant integration with Stripe as the sole payment provider for card payments, ensuring all payment processing occurs via Stripe-hosted fields.
epics.business_value: Enables secure, PCI-DSS-compliant card processing without storing raw card data in the system.

epics.title: Create Payment Record in Pending State Before Redirect
epics.objective: Create a payment record in a 'pending' state before redirecting the customer to the payment provider to ensure order state consistency.
epics.business_value: Provides a clear, traceable state for payment initiation and supports audit logging and failure handling.

epics.title: Exposure and Verification of Stripe Webhook Callbacks
epics.objective: Expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe and verify incoming callbacks using Stripe's signature scheme with a shared secret.
epics.business_value: Ensures secure and authenticated receipt of payment status updates from Stripe, preventing spoofed or malicious messages.

epics.title: Handle Out-of-Order or Duplicate Webhook Deliveries with Idempotency
epics.objective: Implement idempotency to handle out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries without double-crediting an order by deriving a delivery ID from the payload and validating it against a known list of processed IDs with timestamps.
epics.business_value: Prevents double-crediting and maintains data integrity during asynchronous callback processing.

epics.title: Manage Failed Payments and Allow Customer Retry
epics.objective: If a payment fails, mark the order as 'payment failed' and allow the customer to retry payment with the same order, while recording the provider's failure reason code.
epics.business_value: Improves user experience and provides clear failure feedback with actionable retry options.

epics.title: Support Agent-Initiated Refunds for Completed Payments
epics.objective: Enable support agents to issue full or partial refunds for completed payments, with refunds not exceeding the original captured amount.
epics.business_value: Provides operational flexibility for customer service while maintaining financial integrity and compliance.

epics.title: Notify Customers by Email When a Refund is Issued
epics.objective: Deliver a refund notification via SMTP in HTML format with a clear statement such as 'Your refund of $X has been issued for order #Y.'
epics.business_value: Ensures customers are promptly informed of refund actions, improving transparency and trust.

epics.title: Record Immutable Audit Log of All Payment State Transitions
epics.objective: Record every payment state transition (e.g., pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded) in an immutable audit log with a timestamp and actor identification.
epics.business_value: Provides a tamper-proof, traceable record of all payment events for compliance and operational auditing.

epics.title: Ensure Payment Audit Log Retention for Minimum 7 Years
epics.objective: Retain payment audit logs for a minimum of 7 years to meet financial compliance requirements, with the retention period defined as a minimum.
epics.business_value: Meets regulatory compliance for financial data retention and supports long-term audit readiness.

epics.title: Ensure System Resilience to Temporary Stripe API Unavailability
epics.objective: Ensure the system does not lose orders during temporary unavailability of the Stripe API by maintaining order state and processing flow continuity.
epics.business_value: Maintains operational integrity and prevents data loss during transient provider outages.

epics.title: Ensure Webhook Processing Completes Within 2 Seconds Under Normal Load
epics.objective: Process incoming webhook callbacks within 2 seconds under normal load, defined as 100 concurrent requests per second.
epics.business_value: Ensures timely processing of payment status updates, maintaining system responsiveness and reliability.

epics.title: Enforce PCI-DSS Compliance by Preventing Raw Card Data Storage
epics.objective: Ensure that raw card numbers are never stored in the system and that all card entry occurs via Stripe-hosted fields to comply with PCI-DSS scope reduction.
epics.business_value: Eliminates risk of PCI-DSS violations by ensuring no raw card data is ever stored or processed in the system.

epics.title: Define Dependency Between Order Creation and Payment Processing
epics.objective: Ensure payment processing only occurs after the order-creation flow is completed, maintaining correct sequence and data consistency.
epics.business_value: Prevents invalid or incomplete payment attempts by enforcing proper workflow order.

epics.title: Define 'Completed Payment' as a Payment in 'Captured' State with No Further State Changes
epics.objective: Formally define 'completed payment' as a payment that has reached the 'captured' state and has not undergone any further state changes.
epics.business_value: Provides a clear, unambiguous definition for refund eligibility and ensures consistency in payment lifecycle logic.

epics.title: Implement Encrypted, Append-Only Audit Log with Immutable Timestamps and Actor Identification
epics.objective: Store audit logs in encrypted, append-only database entries with immutable timestamps and actor identification to ensure data integrity and prevent tampering.
epics.business_value: Provides a technically sound, immutable record of all payment state transitions for compliance and forensic purposes.

epics.title: Implement Health Check Endpoint to Monitor Stripe API Connectivity
epics.objective: Add a health check endpoint that monitors Stripe API connectivity and alerts operations when the provider is unreachable.
epics.business_value: Improves system resilience by enabling proactive detection and response to Stripe API outages.

epics.title: Add Logging and Monitoring for Webhook Delivery Timestamps and Outcomes
epics.objective: Enhance debugging and compliance by adding detailed logging for webhook delivery timestamps, outcomes, and error codes.
epics.business_value: Supports operational visibility, troubleshooting, and audit trail completeness for payment events.

Expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe, verifying incoming callbacks using Stripe's signature scheme with a shared secret.
Implement idempotency to handle out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries by deriving a delivery ID from the payload and validating it against a known list of processed IDs with timestamps.
If a payment fails, mark the order as 'payment failed' and allow the customer to retry payment with the same order, recording the provider's failure reason code.
Enable support agents to issue full or partial refunds for completed payments, ensuring refunds do not exceed the original captured amount.
Deliver a refund notification via SMTP in HTML format with a clear statement such as 'Your refund of $X has been issued for order #Y.'
Record every payment state transition (e.g., pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded) in an immutable audit log with a timestamp and actor identification.
Retain payment audit logs for a minimum of 7 years to meet financial compliance requirements.
Maintain order state and processing continuity during temporary Stripe API unavailability to prevent order loss.
Process incoming webhook callbacks within 2 seconds under normal load (defined as 100 concurrent requests per second) to ensure timely delivery of payment status updates.
Prevent raw card data storage by ensuring all card entry occurs via Stripe-hosted fields, complying with PCI-DSS scope reduction.
Ensure payment processing only occurs after the order-creation flow is completed to maintain correct sequence and data consistency.
Define 'completed payment' as a payment that has reached the 'captured' state and has not undergone any further state changes to support accurate refund processing.
Store audit logs in encrypted, append-only database entries with immutable timestamps and actor identification to ensure data integrity and prevent tampering.
Add a health check endpoint to monitor Stripe API connectivity and alert operations when the provider is unreachable.
Add detailed logging for webhook delivery timestamps, outcomes, and error codes to support debugging and compliance.
Explicitly ensure that raw card numbers are not stored in the system and that all card entry occurs via Stripe-hosted fields to satisfy PCI-DSS compliance.
Allow customers to create an order and initiate payment for the order total, ensuring the payment initiation flow is accessible and functional.
Define a dependency between order creation and payment processing such that payment processing only occurs after order creation is completed.
Ensure the platform supports asynchronous payment callbacks from Stripe to satisfy the requirement for asynchronous callback handling.
Clarify that the 7-year retention period for payment audit logs is a minimum and apply this definition to the retention policy in US-012.

risks.description: Stripe API may become unavailable during peak traffic, leading to order processing failures.
risks.mitigation: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and a fallback to a local queue for order processing during unavailability.
risks.contingency: Switch to a backup payment provider if Stripe is unavailable for more than 15 minutes.

risks.description: The definition of 'normal load' is not clearly defined, making the 2-second performance requirement difficult to test and validate.
risks.mitigation: Define 'normal load' as 100 concurrent requests per second and validate performance under this condition during testing.
risks.contingency: Use load testing tools to simulate 100 concurrent requests and validate performance metrics in staging.

risks.description: The definition of 'duplicate' webhook delivery is not specified, making idempotency implementation untestable.
risks.mitigation: Derive a delivery ID from the webhook payload and validate it against a known list of processed IDs with timestamps and unique identifiers.
risks.contingency: Implement a database-level audit table to track processed webhook deliveries and validate against it during processing.

risks.description: The definition of 'completed payment' is ambiguous, leading to potential errors in refund processing.
risks.mitigation: Formally define 'completed payment' as a payment that has reached the 'captured' state and has not undergone any further state changes.
risks.contingency: Implement a state machine to validate payment state transitions and ensure only 'captured' payments are eligible for refunds.

risks.description: The email content and format for refund notifications are not specified, leading to potential compliance and customer experience issues.
risks.mitigation: Deliver refund notifications via SMTP in HTML format with a clear statement such as 'Your refund of $X has been issued for order #Y.'
risks.contingency: Use a templated email system with pre-approved content to ensure consistency and compliance.

risks.description: The system may not detect or handle all edge cases in webhook processing, leading to data inconsistencies.
risks.mitigation: Implement comprehensive unit and integration tests for webhook processing scenarios including edge cases.
risks.contingency: Add a manual review process for webhook deliveries that fail validation or exceed processing time thresholds.

risks.description: The shared secret used for webhook signature verification may be compromised if not properly configured at deployment time.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the shared secret is configured securely at deployment time and stored in environment variables with restricted access.
risks.contingency: Rotate the shared secret every 90 days and implement automated rotation with rollback capability.

assumptions.description: The e-commerce platform supports online payments for customer orders, as implied by the overview section.
The platform supports asynchronous callbacks from Stripe, as indicated by the webhook requirement.

issues.description: No explicit story covers raw card data handling and PCI-DSS compliance, violating REQ-002.
No explicit story covers order creation and payment initiation for the customer, violating REQ-006.
No explicit story covers the dependency between order creation and payment processing, violating REQ-018.
No explicit story covers asynchronous callback support from Stripe, violating REQ-022.
The 7-year retention period for audit logs is not clearly defined as a minimum, violating REQ-004.

sprints.sprint_goal: Establish foundational payment flow and ensure PCI-DSS compliance via Stripe integration and data handling.
Implement webhook processing, state consistency, and audit logging with immutability and traceability.
Enable failure recovery and retry mechanisms for customer payments and ensure order continuity during service outages.
Implement refund functionality, notification, and compliance with financial and audit requirements.
Enhance observability, logging, and system health monitoring to support operations and compliance.
Validate all requirements and ensure traceability across security, functional, and operational constraints.
